items.title: Deliver one canonical Finding triage contract to every active REVIEW lane
items.context: Own all REVIEW-lane behavior and prohibitions in one canonical contract: current review_run_start/reviewRunId/finding_add/review_pass_set protocol; independent evidenceState, severity, applicability candidate, and gate-impact axes; fail-closed unknown applicability; evidence-backed routing with owner; no reviewer repair, finding_dismiss, story_create, severity rewriting, or unilateral scope expansion; and distinct disproven, duplicate, and stale-or-not-reproduced outcomes. Deliver identically to all five active REVIEW lanes through both envelope paths and nowhere else.
items.userSees: Generated prompts for all five active REVIEW lanes visibly contain the same complete triage behavior in both supported envelope modes, while non-REVIEW prompts do not.

happy.desc: Assemble each of lattice-review-behavior, lattice-review-concept, lattice-review-docs, lattice-review-quality, and lattice-review-test-coverage in full-envelope mode and prove that every result contains exactly one byte-identical canonical Finding triage contract with the current review_run_start -> reviewRunId -> finding_add or review_pass_set protocol.

Assemble the same five REVIEW roles through legacy-full-context and prove that the identical canonical triage contract is appended exactly once in every result while the role-specific legacy body remains selected.

Inspect the canonical contract and prove that evidenceState, severity, applicability candidate, and gate impact are independent axes; routing requires evidence plus an owner; the machine remains authoritative for blocking; and disproven, duplicate, and stale_or_not_reproduced are separate outcomes.

edge.desc: Exercise mixed per-role rollout selections across the five REVIEW roles and prove every selected prompt receives one complete contract regardless of envelope path, with neither omission nor double injection.

Prove the fail-closed rule is expressed in terms of the current round policy: when applicability is unknown, missing, stale, or untrusted, a Finding that would otherwise block remains blocking, including medium severity in a policy round where medium blocks.
Prove a non-current-Story disposition is allowed only with structured applicability evidence and a traceable owner or route, and that high or critical Findings cannot be left unowned.

Prove the contract preserves the original Finding observation, evidence state, severity, and history: a non-blocking applicability candidate does not resolve or dismiss the Finding and any later severity correction requires append-only revision or supersession rather than silent mutation.

adversarial.desc: Enumerate every active non-REVIEW, compatibility, and retired role and prove none receives the canonical REVIEW triage contract or the defect-triage routing behavior by substring coincidence or broad common-policy injection.

Delete or alter any required protocol command or ordering rule and prove the prompt contract test fails, including review_run_start first, current signed reviewRunId binding, finding_add for a Finding, and review_pass_set only for a valid no-blocker outcome.

Inject wording that lets severity alone decide Story scope, lets an applicability assessment rewrite severity, or equates deferral with finding_dismiss or resolution, and prove semantic validation rejects it.

Inject wording that permits a reviewer to repair implementation, call finding_dismiss, call story_create, or expand the Story merely to make all checks green, and prove semantic validation rejects every permission.

Replace the distinct outcomes with a generic deferred or closed result and prove validation fails unless disproven remains an evidence-truth result, duplicate identifies a canonical live owner, and stale_or_not_reproduced cites current freshness-bound counter-evidence.

Attempt to route an otherwise-blocking unknown-applicability Finding without evidence or owner, or claim that prompt prose itself changes the lifecycle gate, and prove the contract remains fail-closed and non-evidentiary.

items.title: Align Story Owner, implementer, and reviewer authority guidance
items.context: Own only Story Owner disposition and implementer escalation guidance. The Owner returns applicable blockers to DEV, routes evidence-backed non-applicable work without unowned high/critical findings, fails closed when an otherwise-blocking finding has unknown applicability, and treats compatibility dismissal as temporary round/profile handling rather than applicability proof. The implementer preserves reproduction and impact evidence, reports out-of-item findings, and does not widen scope unilaterally.
items.userSees: Story Owner and implementer instructions distinguish current-Story repair from evidence-backed routing and prevent boundaryless scope expansion.

items.title: Register declarative REVIEW triage checks and preserve the Agent-System boundary
items.context: Register defect-triage-and-routing-check only for active REVIEW role contracts. Preserve the Agent/System boundary explicitly: this metadata is declarative, is not proof that a check ran, is not gate evidence, and does not redefine Dynamic Finding schemas, blocking predicates, freshness, supersession, severity, or applicability.
items.userSees: Contract verification shows REVIEW roles declare triage behavior while prompt prose and metadata remain non-evidentiary and do not alter lifecycle gates.

items.title: Prove prompt delivery, isolation, digest integrity, and adapter compatibility
items.context: Use RED then GREEN. Add adversarial tests covering all five REVIEW roles, both full-envelope and legacy-full-context assembly, non-REVIEW isolation, compatibility-dismissal wording, distinct disproven/duplicate/stale routing, English-only prose, and stale in-flight reviewer redispatch guidance. Update approved digest pins, then run focused prompt tests, process/runtime contract checks, prompt baselines, type/build validation, and verify_codex.
items.userSees: A failing pre-implementation contract test becomes green after the change, and digest/adapter verification confirms the published English Agent prompts are fresh and compatible.
